core_obligations: Unwind the definition of an almost free module as one with an exhaustive filtration whose successive quotients are direct sums of shifts of the ring (statement span).
Choose a K-injective or K-projective representative of the bounded below complex so that maps out of the almost free module can be computed degreewise along the filtration (proof span).
Lift the map along the filtration one filtration step at a time, using that the complex is bounded below to kill obstructions in the relevant degrees (proof span).
Conclude the identification of the required mapping group with the corresponding maps of the associated graded module (statement conclusion).
difficulty_reason: The lemma concerns an almost free module in the sense of the surrounding section and a bounded below complex, and identifies the maps out of the former into the latter up to homotopy with the maps of the underlying graded module, using that the almost free module has a filtration whose associated graded pieces are direct sums of free modules shifted (source statement span). The proof has to lift a map defined on the associated graded pieces through the filtration, which uses that the complex is bounded below so that the intervening obstructions vanish one degree at a time; the two cited derived-category lemmas supply the standard step that maps from a projective complex and into an injective complex compute the relevant Hom groups (proof span).
